ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are 7 numbered squares, arranged in a staircase shape: 1, 2, 3 are in the same horizontal row and adjacent from left to right; 4 is above 3; 5 is to the right of 4; 6 is above 5; 7 is to the right of 6. Therefore the movement path in order is: 1→2 to the right, 2→3 to the right, 3→4 upward, 4→5 to the right, 5→6 upward, 6→7 to the right. Reasoning: According to the method, set the bottom face of the die at position 1 as A, the top face as B, the right face as C, the left face as D, the upward-direction face as E, and the downward-direction face as F. When rolling to the right, the original left face goes to the bottom; when rolling upward, the original downward-direction face goes to the bottom. At position 1 the bottom face is A. 1→2 to the right, the bottom face becomes D. 2→3 to the right, the bottom face becomes B. 3→4 upward, the bottom face becomes F. 4→5 to the right, the bottom face becomes C. 5→6 upward, the bottom face becomes A. 6→7 to the right, the bottom face becomes E. The bottom-face sequence is 1:A, 2:D, 3:B, 4:F, 5:C, 6:A, 7:E, so the same face appears at positions 1 and 6.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a path of adjacent squares for the die’s bottom face: from 1 to 2 move right, 2 to 3 right, 3 to 4 up, 4 to 5 right, 5 to 6 up, 6 to 7 right. Assign six symbolic labels to the die’s initial faces at position 1, for example bottom=A, top=B, right=C, left=D, front/up-direction=E, back/down-direction=F. Then update the orientation after each roll: a right roll puts the previous left face on the bottom; an upward roll puts the previous lower/back face on the bottom. Make a table of the bottom face at positions 1 through 7 and identify the repeated symbol. This yields the same bottom symbol at positions 1 and 6.
